summary: Teams of 2-4 students create a 2D computer animation, 1:30 to 2:30 minutes long, telling a story of an object or character that becomes lost, finds its way back, and is changed by the journey. The project includes a storyboard, concept art, works cited, release forms, and AI usage documentation, all submitted in a single PDF. Teams present their work virtually to judges and answer questions about their process.
time_limits: Animation must be at least 1:30 and not exceed 2:30 minutes
Setup: no more than three (3) minutes
Presentation: no more than ten (10) minutes
Judges’ questions: no more than five (5) minutes
Presentation will be stopped at ten (10) minutes
submission_requirements: Submit one combined PDF file containing URL to 2D Animation, Storyboard, Concept Art/Prototype, Works Cited, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form
Submission must be uploaded to https://upload.bpa.org
Team ID is required for all submissions
Materials from non-registered contestants and/or those missing team ID cannot be accepted
deadlines: Event registration deadline: no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, on December 1, 2026
National submission deadline: January 15, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
competencies: Demonstrate proficiency in industry-standard editing software applications to execute all phases of the 2-dimensional animation production process
Develop and sequence animation within a storyboard to communicate a clear and intentional visual narrative
Apply color theory, artistic effects, textures, and special effects to enhance the visual quality and creative impact of animated content
Demonstrate knowledge of transitions, audio, lighting effects, and the proper placement of titles and visual effects to produce a polished, professional final product
Demonstrate an understanding of audience analysis by designing and delivering a final animated product that effectively communicates to a defined target audience

rubric.criterion: Team followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

Team submitted one (1) combined PDF file containing URL to 2D Animation, Storyboard, Concept Art/Prototype Works Cited according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form.

rubric.description: Assets are primarily original and demonstrate creativity and effort in design.
Animation is highly refined, with exceptional attention to detail and technique.
Camera work, timing, and transitions are expertly executed and enhance the project’s impact.
Movement uses squash and stretch expertly to convey weight, volume, and impact.
Anticipation is used effectively and creatively to enhance timing and viewer engagement.
Staging is highly effective, enhancing clarity, emotion, and storytelling.
Movements are fluid and lifelike, with expertly applied slow-in and slow-out.
Secondary actions are thoughtfully integrated, adding depth and realism to the animation.
Concept art and storyboard are highly intentional, detailed, and creatively aligned with project goals.
Contains very few or no grammar or spelling errors.
Animation is highly original, expressive, and showcases fresh, innovative ideas.
Animation is highly engaging, entertaining, and leaves a lasting impression.
Lighting is used creatively and effectively to elevate the visual storytelling.
Audio is crisp, perfectly timed, and enhances the overall experience seamlessly.
Transitions are expertly crafted, enhancing the pacing and visual continuity.

rubric.criterion: Final animation made effective use of time and was within the contest time limit of 1:30 to 2:30 minutes in length.
Team followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: Team is highly confident, expressive, and fully engages the audience throughout.
Thoroughly explains and connects all phases of development to project objectives.
Provides detailed, insightful explanation of innovative tools and techniques used.
Offers a comprehensive and engaging explanation of asset creation and integration.
Provides a thoughtful and detailed explanation of team collaboration and responsibilities.
Presentation style is polished, dynamic, and powerfully enhances audience understanding and engagement.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.

judging_notes: Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level.
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC.
If any required element is answered NO, assign a score of 0 and provide a brief reason for the disqualification.
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring.
Presentation will be stopped at ten (10) minutes.
eligibility_notes: Any middle level, secondary or postsecondary contestant may enter this event.
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants.
There are no restrictions on the number of entries per chapter or per state.
Contestants participating in the competition must be registered for the event prior to the submission deadline to be eligible.
